annotations.text:
Round 2 — the synthesis you picked:

• Header from A, but flat on the surface (no card); the two menus merged into the K button, top-right where the ... was
• View toggle from A
• Buckets from C
• Command bar from B

Two header variants side by side — compact flat vs. C's serif. The Buckets and Command Bar pages (toolbar page menu) explore those two pieces further; Round 1 keeps the original directions.

Flat header

A's compact header sitting straight on the paper — date + week strip with no card around them, so the bucket cards are the only carded thing above the bar. The K menu holds profile, settings, display options and bug report.

Tradeoff: 'Today' at 16px is quiet — the screen has no single dominant element.

Serif header

Same structure, C's voice: the Source Serif headline gives the screen one dominant element and the most distinct brand feel, with the quiet numeral strip underneath.

Tradeoff: tallest header of the two (~14px more), and the serif needs to earn its place on Braindump/Chat too or the app feels split-personality.

1 — Cards (from C)

One white card per bucket on the paper backdrop. Strongest bucket identity and drag targets; what you picked in round 1.
Tradeoff: three borders + three shadows of visual weight, and empty buckets still cost a whole card.

2 — Single sheet (C expanded toward B)

One continuous card holds every bucket as a section, full-width hairlines between sections. Calmest option, most rows per screen, and the sheet edge-to-edge reads like one professional surface.
Tradeoff: weakest bucket boundaries — drop targets and 'which bucket am I in' rely on the section headers alone.

3 — Sheet + spines

The single sheet, but each section carries its time-of-day spine (ported from the desktop bucket cards) instead of hairlines. Keeps the sheet's calm while the tinted spine restores bucket identity and gives drops an edge to land on.
Tradeoff: the spine is subtle at 2px — it must never carry alone what the header says.

4 — Tinted headers

Separate cards, each with a soft time-of-day wash on its header band. Most colorful and glanceable — you can tell Morning from Evening peripherally.
Tradeoff: the washes flirt with the 'lime never dims' discipline — tinted fills need their own dark-mode values, and it is the least Linear-quiet of the four.

1 — Split deck (from B)

Nav segment | input | Beacon in one 56px capsule. Everything is one thumb-reach surface.
Tradeoff: unlabeled icons, and the input gets ~180px of the width — tight once real text is in it. Beacon-as-button also means chat has no 'you are here' state.

2 — Stacked deck

The current dock distilled into one white capsule: full-width input on top, labeled tabs below. Most discoverable — labels survive, capture keeps full width, notices could dock above the input as today.
Tradeoff: tallest option (~96px), so it gives back some of the vertical space the redesign reclaims.

3 — Mode chip

The active surface is a chip inside the input; tapping it opens the switcher, and /braindump, /chat work as typed commands — nav and commands become one vocabulary. Slimmest full-function bar, most Raycast in spirit.
Tradeoff: least discoverable — switching tabs is two taps or a typed command, and swipe becomes the primary gesture.

4 — Nav + capture split

Concerns separated: a slim icons-only nav pill centered, capture as its own lime button (the omnibar opens as a sheet). Cleanest look and the strongest capture affordance.
Tradeoff: capture costs a tap before typing, two floating elements instead of one, and the command palette feels hidden behind a '+' that promises 'add'.

Current (reference)

What ships today: header pill + week-nav pill stacked (two borders, two shadows), then the canvas panel, then the dock well holding notices, omnibar, and tab bar. Five bordered surfaces compete before any content appears — this is why it reads busy rather than professional.

B — Command Deck

Raycast-inspired: chrome nearly disappears. Title and a bare day strip sit straight on paper, content becomes one full-bleed sheet with hairline sections instead of nested cards, and a single bottom capsule owns everything — tab icons, capture ('type to add or command'), and Beacon.

Why: maximal content per screen and the strongest 'powerful tool' feel; one bar is the whole command surface.
Tradeoff: biggest departure — buckets lose their card identity, notices need a new home, and folding chat behind the Beacon button is a navigation change.

C — Editorial Calm

Typography-led quiet: a Source Serif 'Today' headline (the brand's own serif) on bare paper, a numeral day strip with a lime dot, bucket cards floating directly on the backdrop, and an icons-only tab row. Capture moves to a floating lime button that opens the omnibar as a sheet.

Why: the calmest, most 'designed' feel — hierarchy comes from type and spacing, and the cards finally read as the heroes.
Tradeoff: capture is one tap farther away than the always-present omnibar, and the dock's one-voice notice stack loses its anchor.

(A — One Bar evolved into the Synthesis page and no longer appears here.)
